props.name: autocomplete
props.description: Autocomplete hint for the browser and password managers.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: Initial value for the uncontrolled case.

props.name: description
props.description: Persistent helper text below the field.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables interaction. Mirrors the ARIA name.

props.name: error
props.description: The validation message. Its presence drives `aria-invalid`.

props.name: form
props.description: Associates the control with a form it is not nested inside.

props.name: invalid
props.description: Marks the field invalid.  Separate from `error` on purpose: a field can be invalid before the consumer knows why, and an error message can be present without the field being in an error state — for example a form-level summary listing several fields.

props.name: label
props.description: The control's own label text, rendered above the field.

props.name: pattern
props.description: Regular expression the value must match, enforced natively.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Placeholder text. Never a substitute for a label.

props.name: readOnly
props.description: Makes the field non-editable but still submitted and focusable.  Attribute-observed, unlike `disabled`: the HTML attribute name is `readonly` in every case, so Stencil's camelCase-to-kebab mapping cannot be relied on to match it, and a consumer writing `<sk-input readonly>` in plain HTML was silently getting an editable field.

props.name: required
props.description: Native constraint validation still applies and is never suppressed.

props.name: type
props.description: Native input type. Visual configuration stays `variant`/`size` only.

props.name: value
props.description: The value. Uncontrolled by default: typed value only if set.

props.name: name
props.description: The name of the element, used when submitting an HTML form.

ai.summary: A single-line text field that participates in a plain HTML form. Validation is the browser's, not this component's.
whenToUse: The value is a short string: a name, an email, a handle, a search term
It must submit through a plain `<form>` with no JavaScript state
The browser's own constraint validation is wanted rather than a bespoke rules engine
whenNotToUse: The value is long-form text — use a Textarea
The value is one of a fixed set — use a Select or Radio Group
It only toggles a boolean — use a Checkbox or Switch
ai.accessibility: Renders a real native `<input>`, so the browser supplies constraint validation, password managers, autofill, and IME composition rather than this component reimplementing them. `label`, `description`, and `error` are wired through `<label for>` and `aria-describedby`; an error also sets `aria-invalid` and renders an icon beside its text, never color alone (WCAG 1.4.1). `readOnly` keeps the value submitted and focusable, which is what distinguishes it from `disabled`.
knownLimitations: The generated `id` for the inner control differs from React's `useId()`, so an SSR consumer must pass an explicit `id` for a separately-rendered `Label` to find it (section 4, forms contract)
The `pattern` prop takes a string, not a RegExp, because it becomes a native attribute
